newsitem.title: UK: Fiery dollar hits 3-1/2 year high against yen.
newsitem.headline: Fiery dollar hits 3-1/2 year high against yen.

text.p: The dollar leaped to its best levels against the yen for three-and-a-half years in Europe on Monday, as yield-hungry investors dumped the Japanese currency across the board.

The pound, the mark and the Australian and New Zealand dollars all reaped rich rewards from the yen's slide. Against the mark, the dollar was consigned to well-trodden ranges, capped by fading expectations of German interest rate cuts.
Analysts said differentials between interest rates and bond yields conspired with technical factors and an uncertain Japanese political situation to hit the yen.
Japan's general election on October 20 produced a hung parliament, and the potential coalition partners have as yet failed to form a new government.
Most bets are now on Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto going into the new parliamentary session as the head of a minority government -- making fresh elections a constant threat.
"The political situation is uneasy at the moment and while that's going on there's no chance of the Bank of Japan moving up rates," said David Bloom, U.S. economist at HSBC James Capel.
The dollar's breach of the key 113.58 yen level -- its high from January 1994 -- set pulses racing among technical analysts, who use charts to predict future price movements.
That break accelerated the U.S. unit's upmove and propelled it to 114.15 yen by 1217 GMT, off an earlier high of 114.30 but far above late Friday's European level of 113.24.
Technical analysts looked for a test of a trendline at 114.50 ahead of support-turned-resistance at 115.00 and 115.85.

The economic dynamics continue to favour yen weakness, economists argued. Japan's trade account is set to deteriorate further, while the fiscal and monetary bias is towards further easing to stoke up growth, they said.
The mark surged against the yen to touch 74.98, its strongest rate since February 1993.
That weighed on dollar/mark, which was already firmly capped by diminishing hopes of near-term German rate cuts.

Bundesbank members queued up on Friday to suggest that while there was no current need to ease policy, rate reductions were not definitively off the agenda. But the German central bank's president Hans Tietmeyer quashed the dollar's upbeat reaction by saying he saw no need for cuts in the foreseeable future.

"It should be noted that the two heavyweights, Tietmeyer and (Bundesbank chief economist Otmar) Issing, were the least bullish on rate cut scope," said Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
"It is a sign of the rather feeble momentum of dollar/mark that it can only hold on to current levels, let alone rally, on the basis of rate cut expectations in Germany," he added.
The dollar stood at 1.5235 marks at European midsession, only slightly firmer than late Friday's level of 1.5192.

No U.S. data were due on Monday, but the market was awaiting a raft of figures beginning Tuesday with the third-quarter employment cost index, known to be closely watched by the U.S. Federal Reserve whose next policy meeting is on November 13.

Other key U.S. releases include third-quarter GDP out Wednesday and personal income and spending data Thursday. The biggest attention-grabber of them all, however, is the October non-farm payrolls report scheduled to appear on Friday.
Sterling put in a sparkling performance during the European morning, scaling a 16-month peak of $1.6145 and hitting 2.4590 marks, its strongest level there since December 1995.
Sterling/yen's gains were even more impressive. It touched 184.28 yen, an area not glimpsed seen since February 1993.
